newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Nortel, Williams to combine sales arms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nortel, Williams to combine sales arms.

text.p: Williams Communications Group Inc. and Northern Telecom Ltd. agreed on Thursday to merge their subsidiaries that sell and service telephone equipment to corporations.

The merged entity, comprising Nortel's Canadian and U.S. distribution arms -- TTS Meridian Systems Inc. and Nortel Communications Systems Inc. -- and Williams' distribution unit, will be based in Houston and called WilTel Communications LLC.
WilTel, to be 70 percent-held by Williams and 30 percent by Nortel, would provide customized telecommunications systems for corporate customers across North America.
Williams Communications is a unit of Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams Cos. Inc..
Nortel will get an undisclosed amount of cash, which analysts estimated at a couple of hundred million dollars. Completion is set to occur in 30 to 45 days.
The three units have 6,000 employees and annual sales topping $1 billion.
The deal will get Brampton, Ontario-based Nortel out of the business of selling private branch exchange (PBX) switches and telephones to corporate customers in North America.
Analysts were unsure about the benefits of the deal.
"Nortel, if they can stick with a distribution strategy more than a year, it would be a good thing," said Christopher Thompson, a telecommunications analyst at San Jose, Calif.-based DataQuest.
He said Nortel only two years ago acquired the businesses it is merging into WilTel.
Thompson said the deal would allow Nortel to provide better service to companies on both sides of the border.
But he added there were two possible drawbacks to the deal -- WilTel's reputation with corporate customers and a possible negative reaction from other distributers who sell Nortel equipment.
"It's also questionable now if I am a Nortel Communications Systems customer whether I would want to be a WilTel customer. WilTel doesn't have a good name here in the U.S.," Thompson said.

"My gut feel is that WilTel's ability to execute today is very good and that customer perceptions are based more on historical events. Nevertheless, that could affect a significant number of customers," he added.
Thompson also said that many distributors of Nortel products in the corporate market competed with WilTel and could draw away from Nortel because of its union with a rival.
